attractions.name: Margalla Hills National Park
attractions.description: A forested national park bordering the city, with numerous hiking trails (Trail 3, Trail 5, and more) offering views over Islamabad.

attractions.name: Daman-e-Koh
attractions.description: A hilltop viewpoint within the Margalla Hills offering panoramic views of Islamabad, popular for sunset visits.

attractions.name: Pir Sohawa & Monal Restaurant
attractions.description: A scenic hilltop road above the city with popular restaurants offering panoramic dining views over Islamabad.

attractions.name: Rawal Lake
attractions.description: A large reservoir on the edge of the city popular for boating, walking trails, and picnics.

attractions.name: Saidpur Village
attractions.description: A restored centuries-old village at the foot of the Margalla Hills, with heritage architecture, temples, and cafes.

food_places.name: Monal Restaurant
food_places.specialty: Hilltop dining with panoramic views over Islamabad

food_places.name: Saidpur Village cafes
food_places.specialty: Restored heritage village setting with cafes and restaurants

travel_tips.tip: Spring (March-April) and autumn offer the most pleasant weather for sightseeing in Islamabad.
Ride-hailing apps (Careem, InDrive) are the easiest way to get around; the Metro Bus is a cheap option between Islamabad and Rawalpindi.
Zone III is one of five planning zones in Islamabad Capital Territory — attractions here are grouped by zone rather than by separate towns.

history.founded: Designated as Islamabad's protected rural/green development zone, encompassing the Margalla Hills
history.city_history: Zone III was set aside largely for conservation and low-density development, and contains the Margalla Hills National Park and Rawal Lake — Islamabad's main natural attractions.
history.province_history: Islamabad was purpose-built starting in 1960 as Pakistan's new capital, replacing Karachi, and was inaugurated in 1967. Designed by Greek architect Constantinos Doxiadis on a grid of numbered sectors at the foot of the Margalla Hills, it is one of the few purpose-planned capital cities in South Asia.
